description: Share one libsql connection handle across storage calls (get_conn clones an Arc instead of re-opening the DB file per call)

asi.hypothesis: libsql Database::connect() re-opens the sqlite file for the local backend; ~10 calls per recall query each paid an open. Connection is Arc<dyn Conn> + derive(Clone), so one handle cloned per call removes ~10 file opens per query with zero SQL changes.
asi.expected: warm p95 418ms -> well under 300ms; cold cli/mcp p95 also drop since each process makes many calls

score graph candidates by distance-decayed path strength instead of a constant

asi.hypothesis: Fusion paid every graph neighbour the same bonus (strength pinned to 1.0, depth min-ed to 1), so on a hub the weakly-linked high-importance noise crowded out the strongly-linked answer. Carrying edge strength through the walk and scoring distance-decayed path strength should let the strong edge win.
asi.next: If the crowding query still fails, the blocker is the importance prior outranging the graph channel (w_graph * 0.9 vs importance_weight * 0.6 spread), not the traversal signal; then decide between reweighting channels and a fixture whose noise importance is not uniformly maximal.
